acceptanceGates.requirement: Tokenizer corpus manifest is sealed and hashed.
Tokenizer artifact vocabulary size is exactly 8192.
Required special tokens exist exactly once with stable IDs recorded in the tokenizer manifest.
Compression/token-count evaluation is performed on held-out representative text.
D0 checkpoint and embedded tokenizer remain byte-identical and untouched.

acceptance: German round-trip including umlauts and ß
byteCoverage.requirement: Tokenizer must retain a byte-level fallback path capable of representing arbitrary valid UTF-8 input without depending on the D0 42-character alphabet.

contract.purpose: Define tokenizer ownership, corpus requirements, special-token semantics, reproducibility requirements and acceptance gates before D1 tokenizer training.

minimumPlanningFloor.description: 10 MB is a readiness floor for the first D1 tokenizer experiment, not a claim that 10 MB is sufficient for final D1 language-model training.

preferredInitialTarget.description: Aim for at least approximately 100 MB of diverse, clean text for the first serious 8K tokenizer candidate when legally available.

requirements: corpus must be Denarixx-controlled or legally usable
every source must have provenance metadata
raw corpus must be immutable after manifest sealing
processed corpus must be independently versioned
all corpus artifacts used for tokenizer training must be SHA-256 hashed
duplicate and near-duplicate analysis must occur before final tokenizer corpus sealing
UTF-8 decoding failures must be reported
tokenizer corpus must materially exceed the D0 research corpus
evaluation text must not be intentionally copied into tokenizer training solely to improve benchmark results

prohibitions: do not reuse D0 42-character vocabulary as D1 vocabulary
do not download pretrained tokenizer vocabulary
do not silently change target vocabulary size
do not silently change special-token contract
do not train tokenizer before corpus readiness is measured
do not train D1 model before tokenizer acceptance gates pass

tokenizer.normalizationPolicy: preserve source Unicode text; no lossy ASCII-only normalization
